principles: Single source of truth: one invariant fn, never a third copy of the relative-path escape check
Fail early and loudly with actionable remediation, but do not retroactively break setups that work today
Keep the two existing late guards as the hard backstop (defense in depth)
The normal case (metadataRoot == gitRoot) must be byte-identical and free of false-positive advisories
drivers: Users invest full INIT + PLAN effort before discovering the dead end at INIT_CHECK
Wrapper-root layouts (configured gitRoot at a subdir) are a real, supported configuration
Divergent copies of the escape check would drift and reintroduce the bug

options.name: A: advisory + doctor (warn, non-blocking)
pros: Non-breaking: existing wrapper-root projects keep working
Surfaces the problem early with exact remediation
Late guards still hard-stop the actually-broken operation
cons: A user can ignore the warning and still hit the late guard at INIT_CHECK

options.name: B: hard-fail at story_create
pros: Impossible to invest PLAN work in a doomed setup
cons: Retroactively breaks existing wrapper-root projects (e.g. ClawCreek created 19 stories fine before any such gate)
story_create has no such gate today; adding one is a behavior break

options.name: C: auto-relocate storyDir into gitRoot
cons: Dangerous magic: moves files, risks collisions, surprising side effects
Out of scope for a detection/advisory story

rationale: Option A surfaces the violation early (doctor + a story_create/session_brief advisory) with the exact remediation, while keeping the two late guards as the hard backstop. It does not retroactively break existing wrapper-root projects that limp along today. B trades that safety for a worse migration story; C is dangerous magic. A is the minimal, reversible, non-breaking improvement. Resolves unknown #1 (warn, not hard-fail) and unknown #2 (surface on BOTH doctor and the story_create/session_brief advisory, since users look at session_brief Next-step output).

preMortem.scenario: The advisory is too quiet and users still hit the late guard
preMortem.trigger: Warning is buried in noisy story_create output
preMortem.consequence: No real improvement over the status quo for that user
preMortem.mitigation: Have doctor flag it as a distinct failed check (non-zero/clearly marked) and place the advisory on the session_brief surface users actually read

preMortem.scenario: The extracted shared fn diverges from the two guards during refactor
preMortem.trigger: A subtle realpath/normalization difference creeps in
preMortem.consequence: Guard behavior changes, breaking valid setups or admitting broken ones
preMortem.mitigation: Refactor both guards to call the shared fn; add a test asserting it flags the exact ClawCreek case and passes for metadataRoot == gitRoot

preMortem.scenario: The advisory false-positives on the normal case
preMortem.trigger: metadataRoot == gitRoot relative path mis-computed (e.g. symlink)
preMortem.consequence: Every normal project sees a spurious warning
preMortem.mitigation: realpath both sides; add tests for no-configured-gitRoot and metadataRoot == gitRoot returning ok

preMortem.scenario: The doctor check throws when gitRoot is unresolvable
preMortem.trigger: configured gitRoot missing or not a git repo
preMortem.consequence: doctor crashes instead of reporting the problem
preMortem.mitigation: Guard the check: if signed-workspace resolution is unresolved, report that condition separately and never throw
